name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_THELIVINGWORLD_MCQ_Q01 - Ascending sequence of hierarchical taxonomic categories

questiontext.text:
Arrange the following taxonomic categories in the correct ascending order of the taxonomic hierarchy:

  1. Class
  2. Genus
  3. Order
  4. Species
  5. Family

Choose the correct sequence from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the definition of ascending taxonomic hierarchy.
Taxonomic hierarchy is the arrangement of taxonomic categories in a definite order. An ascending order proceeds progressively from the lowest, most specific category to the highest, most inclusive category.

Step 2: Recall the universal hierarchy of taxonomic ranks.
The standard ascending sequence of major taxonomic categories is: Species → Genus → Family → Order → Class → Phylum (or Division) → Kingdom.

Step 3: Map and arrange the given categories.
Among the given categories: - Species represents the lowest, fundamental rank. - Genus represents an aggregate of closely related species. - Family comprises a group of related genera. - Order represents an assemblage of families exhibiting a few common features. - Class is the highest rank among the given categories, uniting related orders.

Step 4: Formulate the final order.
Arranging these categories in ascending sequence yields: Species → Genus → Family → Order → Class, which corresponds to the sequence IV → II → V → III → I.
